requirements.name: Distinct additive identities
requirements.text: Track local planning IDs tumbler and midnight_man as two additional families; Man is an alias, not a third family. No canonical runtime IDs are assigned.

requirements.name: Availability boundary
requirements.text: Tumbler is explicitly World 1. Midnight Man is a planned playable lead with world/release availability and unlock pending.

requirements.name: Historical preservation
requirements.text: Retain the prior 99-family, 27-ladder, 54-stage, seven-image, 24-panel snapshot and all its receipts. Keep the historical 38 conditional briefs distinct from two new upgrade-disposition-pending families.

requirements.name: Source-defined Tumbler baseline
requirements.text: Retain twin horizontal flat front cutters, eligible enemy/tree/all-mineable contact, named paid-camp cutter safety, explicit player Launch, up to 10 distinct eligible enemies, assigned-target homing, and one shared 3-second cooldown after a successful volley.

requirements.name: Source-defined Tumbler custody
requirements.text: Retain the armored rear hatch above the turbine, typed custody, exactly-once warehouse unload and existing inside/outside wreck rules. Logs/crate imagery is not a capacity specification.

requirements.name: No unspecified vehicle inheritance
requirements.text: Scope old generic vehicle baseline prose to Snow Truck. Do not infer Tumbler fuel/power source, unlimited capacity, hull/garage fit, unlock, price or balance. VC01/VC02 remain unresolved.

requirements.name: Source-defined Midnight Man baseline
requirements.text: Keep his auto-targeted batarangs and the Sweep, Breakthrough and proposed Rebound sequences character-specific; do not change standard player orbiting axes or survivor two-handed tools.

requirements.name: Open character controls
requirements.text: Throw trigger, target priority, cadence, damage, range, controls and unlock remain open; Rebound hybrid versus all-melee remains undecided.

requirements.name: Real future purchase value
requirements.text: Any later upgrade proposal must name the existing baseline limitation, an actual additional capability or measurable gain, its visible mechanism, input/action/output flow, footprint/access consequences, requirements and tradeoff. Existing baseline abilities cannot be sold as newly unlocked upgrades.

requirements.name: No new tiers or balance figures
requirements.text: This delta defines no equipment level, appearance tier, new price, damage/range number, fuel/capacity figure or unlock level. The 10-target limit and 3-second cooldown are quoted source design values, not new authored tuning.

requirements.name: Task identity preservation
requirements.text: Keep exact existing T01-T80 names and dependency arrays. Create only a named local unassigned Midnight Man implementation/review work item, not an invented T-number or reused Character 1-4 gate.

requirements.name: Native evidence remains separate
requirements.text: Before gameplay support, require source-specific actual models/rigs/actions, normal-camera footage, target and custody/event tests, audio and applicable reference/device gates. No art/native/release approval is claimed.

requirements.name: Existing settlement scope
requirements.text: Preserve 10 worlds x 50 levels, storage-house purchase value, multiple pets/survivors, paid loss/recovery boundaries and selected ordinary conveyor/resource unit scale.

requirements.name: Image evidence limit
requirements.text: The two new JPG references are pinned by Git tree identity only in this reconciliation. No new image was generated or visually inspected, and no prior image score is reused.

acceptance_checklist.requirement: Four exact source-text snapshots match their manifest Git blobs.
Counts reconcile 99+2=101; vehicles 1+1=2; human actors 10+1=11; playable identities 4+1=5; old ladders/stages/images/panels remain unchanged.
Every mapped task name and dependency array matches the retained task delta; no new Txx or runtime ID is assigned.
Independent review checks this additive delta against exact source snapshots and preservation boundaries.
Inspect the two actual pinned reference images before making visual-identity or modeling claims.
Future appearance/value briefs distinguish real additional gains from published baseline abilities, with explicit mechanisms, requirements, tradeoffs and access/flow.
Tumbler cutters show valid contacts against eligible enemies, trees and every mineable type including slate and coal, while retaining paid-camp cutter safety.
Tumbler volley tests cover 0/1/10/>10 eligible enemies, distinct assignments, assigned-target homing, no launch without player input and the shared 3-second cooldown after successful volleys.

Tumbler typed cargo, blocked unload, exactly-once warehouse receipt and inside/outside wreck handling remain conserved through save/reload; no render-derived capacity or unspecified power system is assumed.
Actual Tumbler hull/cutter/hatch envelope and garage/storage receiving/dispatch paths fit with service access and both pedestrian camp routes preserved.
Midnight Man throw control/priority/cadence and Rebound hybrid-versus-melee decision are explicitly authored before final animation/control acceptance.
An actual Midnight Man rig plus full Sweep, Breakthrough, Rebound and throw clips show windup/contact/recovery at normal native camera; review all meaningful angles, contacts and full cycles.
Midnight Man chooses eligible combat/harvest targets and produces one harvest receipt per accepted event, including interruption and save/reload regression.
Four existing leads, standard orbiting axes, survivor two-handed tools and separate pet/survivor roles remain unchanged in the released candidate.
Canonical identity, availability, acquisition/recovery and balance decisions are source-bound; Midnight Man has an explicitly assigned implementation/review owner without repurposing T59-T61.
The exact release containing each asset passes applicable reference, ordinary-player economy, audio, accessibility, performance and physical-device gates; prior receipts are not extended.
